title: API Metrics and Monitoring
learning_outcomes: Explain how api metrics and monitoring affects an API contract or implementation.
Apply the key ideas from request rate, errors, and latency to a concrete API example.
Identify one failure, security, or compatibility risk and describe how to verify it.

content.intro: This lesson focuses on api metrics and monitoring in deployment, monitoring, and operations. You will connect request rate, errors, and latency to a concrete API contract decision, inspect a small example, and decide what evidence proves the behavior is correct.
content.why_it_matters: API Metrics and Monitoring matters because API consumers depend on predictable behavior even when clients, servers, networks, and stored data evolve independently. Applying request rate, errors, and latency deliberately reduces ambiguity, makes failures easier to diagnose, and gives tests a clear expectation.

content_blocks.title: Lesson 207 concept map
content_blocks.alt_text: Lesson 207: Request rate, errors, and latency → Percentile response times → Dependency and database metrics → Dashboards and alert thresholds.
content_blocks.caption: Follow the 4 syllabus topics in order, then inspect the example.

content_blocks.title: Core idea
content_blocks.text: Production operation requires reproducible configuration, TLS, health signals, actionable telemetry, and a tested recovery process. In this lesson, treat “API Metrics and Monitoring” as a design or implementation decision: name the expected behavior, identify its boundary, and verify it with a representative request or test.

content_blocks.title: Inspect the pattern: API Metrics and Monitoring
content_blocks.expected_output: Structured logs use stable fields and a correlation identifier while avoiding authorization headers, credentials, and unnecessary personal data.

content_blocks.title: Walkthrough
content_blocks.text: Start with “Request rate, errors, and latency”; it establishes the vocabulary for this topic. Next, compare it with “Percentile response times” and “Dashboards and alert thresholds”. In a real API, write down the observable behavior first, then test one normal request and one invalid or unauthorized request. Keep resource state, caller identity, and internal implementation details separate.

content_blocks.title: Professional review check
content_blocks.text: A successful deployment is not complete until operators can detect and recover from failures. The worked snippet is intentionally inspectable, not an executable hosted API. Replace example.test and placeholder identifiers with local test data only when you implement the lesson project.

content.task: Create a small design note or request/response example demonstrating api metrics and monitoring. Use the subtopics above to explain the intended behavior, the main edge case, and the evidence you would use to verify it.
task_acceptance_criteria: Explain the role of “Request rate, errors, and latency” in this API topic.
Provide a concrete resource, request, response, schema, test, or operational example as appropriate.
Identify one failure/security/compatibility edge case and a test or check for it.
content.expected_output: A reviewable example for API Metrics and Monitoring with a clear expected behavior and at least one verifiable edge case.
content.run_instructions: Execution mode: static-validation. This lesson example is a protocol, schema, SQL, or code fragment for inspection; it is not submitted to a production server and CodeLeaf does not execute arbitrary learner code. Validate JSON/YAML with a local linter or run the relevant HTTP request against the isolated service you implement for a project. Do not send illustrative example.test requests to a real service.
content.reset_steps: Use a disposable local database or test fixture for implementation work. Restore seed data between runs; never point exercises at production customer data or live payment endpoints.
troubleshooting: Check the exact HTTP method, path, status, header, media type, and payload before changing implementation code.
Separate a transport failure from an application validation failure, authorization denial, and dependency/database failure.
Confirm the example and its client tooling version are compatible; consult the linked standard or official guidance when behavior is ambiguous.
common_mistakes: Treating api metrics and monitoring as an implementation detail rather than a documented behavior.
Testing only the happy path and ignoring malformed, unauthorized, conflicting, duplicate, or dependency-failure cases.
Publishing an example without checking version assumptions, sensitive-data exposure, and the expected output.
summary: Production operation requires reproducible configuration, TLS, health signals, actionable telemetry, and a tested recovery process. In this lesson, treat “API Metrics and Monitoring” as a design or implementation decision: name the expected behavior, identify its boundary, and verify it with a representative request or test.
Next, connect this idea to Lesson 208: Distributed Tracing.
